title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page continues a classical, analytic description of elliptic curves and their families, apparently as a warm-up before treating the algebraic moduli stack of elliptic curves away from characteristic 2.

The previous page sets up the data. An elliptic curve E over C is given by its lattice H = H_1(E,Z) together with a complex structure on V = H⊗R, which is identified with the tangent space t_E. Over a complex-analytic base S, this becomes a rank-2 local system 𝓗 of Z-modules. The real-analytic bundle 𝓗⊗R carries a structure of complex line bundle such that the local sections of 𝓗 are holomorphic.

On this page:

(3) Suppose z1, z2 are local sections of 𝓗 forming a fibrewise R-basis of 𝓗⊗R. Then such a complex structure is equivalent to the function τ = z2/z1, viewed as a section of O_S. The NB explains why. For a given complex structure, z1 and z2 are two nowhere-vanishing (basis) sections of the resulting invertible sheaf, and τ is the holomorphic function relating them:

(3bis) z2 = τ z1.

A marginal note adds that τ(s) ∈ C∖R for all s ∈ S. This is because z1 and z2 are R-independent in a complex line.

Conversely, any holomorphic τ: S → C∖R defines the complex structure in which z1 = 1 and z2 = τ. So the period map τ classifies the Hodge-type data.

(4) A 'Torelli structure' on a relative elliptic curve E/S is a trivialisation t: Z_S^2 ≅ 𝓗, that is, a global frame (z1, z2) of 𝓗; in modern terms, a marking or homology framing. The category of relative elliptic curves over S with Torelli structure is rigid: no object has a non-identity automorphism. This holds because an automorphism respecting the frame acts trivially on H_1 and hence is the identity.

The next page completes the picture. Isomorphism classes correspond to holomorphic maps τ: S → C∖R. 'Strict' Torelli structures are those where (z1, z2) is positively oriented for the complex orientation; these correspond to maps to the upper half-plane D+. The universal family is (D+×C)/Z^2, with fibres C/(Z+Zτ) ≅ C*/q^Z where q = exp(2πiτ).

So the page establishes, in Grothendieck's language of fibred categories, the standard fact that the marked (framed) analytic moduli problem is fine. It is represented by C∖R (two copies of the upper half-plane, one per orientation), or by D+ in the oriented case. This sets up the quotient by SL2(Z)/GL2(Z) to get the moduli stack.
errors: No substantive error. Minor imprecision: in (3), 'section of O_S' should be qualified as a holomorphic function with values in C∖R. The margin note supplies the C∖R condition.
The NB parenthesis is opened but never closed in the manuscript. A 'il faut' is struck out mid-sentence; this is a draft artifact.

ideas.what: A complex structure on the real rank-2 bundle 𝓗⊗R making 𝓗 holomorphic is equivalent to a holomorphic period ratio τ = z2/z1 with values in C∖R.
ideas.modern_name: Period map / variation of Hodge structure of weight 1 for families of elliptic curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weierstrass/Jacobi periods); in VHS language Griffiths (1960s)

ideas.what: A Torelli structure (global frame of H_1) rigidifies the moduli problem: objects have no non-trivial automorphisms.
ideas.modern_name: Marked/framed elliptic curves; rigidification by level/marking structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical Teichmüller-style marking; level structures rigidifying: Mumford, Deligne–Rapoport
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the Teichmüller-space discussion in Grothendieck's Séminaire Cartan exposés (1960–61), but unsure

ideas.what: Fine moduli space for marked analytic elliptic curves is C∖R, or D+ for oriented markings, with universal family (D+×C)/Z^2 (on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: Upper half-plane as Teichmüller space of genus 1; universal elliptic curve over the half-plane

deep.surprise_reason: Textbook material (the period ratio, the marked moduli problem, the upper half-plane), written out in Grothendieck's fibred-category style as a preliminary for the moduli stack of elliptic curves. Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'du faisceau inversible Ω[?]' should probably read '... sections-bases du faisceau inversible obtenu' (the line bundle obtained from the complex structure), not Ω.

'structure presque[?] complexe' is doubtful. The image seems to read '+ structure complexe sur 𝓗⊗R'; the illegible word before the colon on the preceding line is likely 'équivaut à' or similar, not 'presque'.
'est [-équivalente à-] {+"rigide"+}': the struck-out word looks like 'équivalente à', with '"rigide"' written above it; this reading is consistent with the transcription.
